items.title: NATO reportedly hopes US will delay European troop withdrawal decision
items.summary: Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources, reported that NATO expects Washington to postpone a decision on withdrawing some US troops from Europe as the Trump administration focuses on Ukraine peace negotiations. The sources also cited improved relations over allied defence spending. No formal postponement was announced.

items.title: Latvian prime minister criticizes Estonia's Russian border transport decision
items.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Kulbergs reportedly described Estonia's decision to close transport links at the Russian border as a mistake, urging consideration of how traffic could be redirected through neighboring countries.

items.title: Renewed strikes reported in Kyiv
items.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reportedly confirmed a strike on a warehouse. Separate accounts alleged damage to energy infrastructure and reported a fire. The full extent of damage has not been independently established.

items.title: Protests reportedly follow prolonged power outages in Dnipro
items.summary: Local social media accounts reportedly described residents blocking streets after prolonged electricity outages. A city council deputy said some districts had experienced outages lasting two to three days, with generators unable to fully meet apartment buildings' electricity and heating needs.

items.title: Putin highlights national-currency trade with Kazakhstan
items.summary: Meeting Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Moscow, Vladimir Putin said bilateral trade had exceeded $28 billion and more than 90% of settlements were conducted in national currencies. He also outlined opportunities for cooperation in artificial intelligence and other high-tech industries.
